label: sec:categorical-point-explication
title: Points in the archimedean realisation
html:
Points in the archimedean realisation.

In the archimedean realisation A = \mathcal{O}(G), a categorical point p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A is a character \mathrm{ev}_g \colon f \mapsto f(g) for some g \in G; equivalently, a point of the group G. For a manifold M with A = C^{\infty}(M), a point p corresponds to evaluation at p \in M:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:point-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \{*\} \ar[r, "p"]
  & M
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\longleftrightarrow\qquad
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "p"]
  & A
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}

The augmentation ideal at p is \mathfrak{m}_p = \ker(p^* \colon A \to \mathbf{1}), where p^* = \int_A \circ \mu(p \otimes -). The germ of A at p is the quotient A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2, which captures the first-order behaviour of A near p.
